deep.reconstruction:
This is the first preserved page of Grothendieck's axiomatic sketch of 'topologie modérée' (tame topology). The setting appears to be the following. R is a real (ordered) field, perhaps R itself, and R_0 is a distinguished subfield of 'constants'. M is a class of 'moderate' subsets of the spaces R^n (or R^I) satisfying axioms M1..M8. Moderate spaces and moderate maps are built from these.

The page first fixes the notation 𝔻 for functions on an ind-moderate space X. Axiom M8 says R is the union (filtered colimit) of its moderate parts. Hence the R^I are not moderate in general but ind-moderate spaces, i.e. ind-objects of the category of moderate spaces. On them one has the ring of ind-moderate functions. This ring contains the coordinate functions and the polynomial ring R_0[(X_i)_{i∈I}].

A marginal addition strengthens this. R_0-polynomial maps R^I → R^J are moderate, and they map moderate parts to moderate parts. This is the analogue of the fact that images of semialgebraic or definable sets under polynomial maps are again semialgebraic or definable.

Corollary 1. For a moderate function f on a moderate space X, f is a unit in the ring of moderate functions iff f has no zero on X.

By replacing X with f(X) ⊂ R^*, this reduces to Corollary 2. If A ⊂ R^* and A ∈ M, then the graph of inversion on A, {(x,x^{-1}) : x ∈ A} ⊂ R^2, is in M.

The next page gives the proof. The graph is the fibre over 1 of the moderate map (x,y) ↦ xy restricted to A×B. Here B is a moderate set assumed to contain A^{-1}, and the fibre over a point is moderate. The next page then deduces that R_0 is a subfield of R; presumably R_0 is the set of 'moderate constants', i.e. points whose singleton is moderate. It then passes to describing moderate subsets as common zero sets of moderate functions.

In modern terms, this is the elementary closure lemma in o-minimal / definable geometry. Definable functions with no zeros have definable reciprocals, and the definable closure of the empty set is a subfield.
errors: Possible gap: if moderate sets are 'bounded' — which M8 and the need for ind-moderate R^I suggest — Corollary 1 is false as stated. Take A=(0,1] ⊂ R^*: its inverse image [1,∞) is unbounded, so the graph of x↦1/x on A lies in no moderate B×A. The proof on the next page explicitly assumes a moderate B containing A^{-1}, so Grothendieck seems aware of this. Without that assumption the statement only holds in the ring of ind-moderate functions, or for A bounded away from 0.

The reduction 'considering f(X) ⊂ R^*' uses tacitly that images of moderate sets under moderate maps are moderate, and that moderate functions compose with the inversion graph. These are presumably among axioms M1-M8, which are not on this page.

ideas.what: Ind-moderate spaces: R and R^I as filtered unions (ind-objects) of moderate parts, carrying rings of ind-moderate functions
ideas.modern_name: ind-definable / locally definable spaces; locally semialgebraic spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (locally semialgebraic spaces, 1985); ind-definable sets in model theory (Hrushovski, Edmundo and others)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for a 'topologie modérée' without this formalism

ideas.what: Polynomial maps with coefficients in R_0 are moderate and preserve moderate sets (axiom-level closure)
ideas.modern_name: closure of definable sets under images of definable maps (Tarski–Seidenberg in semialgebraic case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tarski, Seidenberg; o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight

ideas.what: A moderate function without zeros is invertible in the ring of moderate functions; graph of inversion on a moderate A ⊂ R^* is moderate
ideas.modern_name: definable functions are closed under reciprocal where nonzero
dcl(∅) is a (real closed) subfield in an o-minimal expansion of a field

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates tame topology from the outset with an ind-object layer: moderate sets are 'small' (bounded-like) and R^I are ind-moderate. This is a categorical framing different from the usual o-minimal one, where R^n itself is definable. It anticipates locally definable / ind-definable spaces, apparently independently and possibly before Delfs–Knebusch, depending on the uncertain dating.
missed.quote: si R est réunion de ses parties modérées (M8) i.e. les R^I des espaces ind-modérés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest only. It documents that Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics were built around bounded 'moderate' sets plus ind-completion, which is closer to bornological / locally definable formalisms than to standard o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary closure properties of a definable-set-like structure. The only notable feature is the ind-moderate framing and the early, independent axiomatics of tame topology, which is historically interesting but not new mathematics.
